Rozprza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rozprza, Poland

Not demolished. Rozprza, founded before 1272 and demoted from city status in 1870, saw Jewish settlement from the 17th century, with a kehilla by century's end; population reached 62% (557) by 1897, still roughly 60% by the early 20th century. A synagogue was built in 1898; during WWII, all residents were transported to the Piotrków Trybunalski ghetto. This cemetery, per some unconfirmed sources founded in 1677, originally also served nearby Piotrków Trybunalski's Jews. Germans repurposed matzevot to pave stable and barn floors; postwar theft for construction and grindstones followed. A 2013 local effort uncovered and replaced the missing matzevah of Rojza Lea Prager; a 2014 cleanup by the local volunteer fire brigade, Piotr Skrobek, and Jonny Daniels' From The Depths Foundation ('Matzevah' project) recovered about 20 tombstones or fragments, several re-erected upright, including the notably well-preserved polychrome-decorated tombstone of Icchak, son of Elchanan Efraim ha-Lewi Różycki.
